outcome: No resolution, no new unconditional case, and no AI involvement of the actual section conjecture (as stated: complete smooth curves over finitely-generated fields, splittings to the Galois group) has been found in the window 26 January 2024 to 22 September 2026; the surjectivity direction remains explicitly described as wide open, and the papers found in the window address either variants (analogues over C, toric/birational fundamental groups) or pre-window special cases.
summary: I re-ran and expanded the triage's searches (general 'section conjecture' progress queries, arXiv-specific searches, Stix/Betts author searches, and an explicit AI/machine-learning search) and found an active but narrow literature since 26 January 2024, none of which changes what a careful person would write in this bullet. (1) Bresciani's 'On Grothendieck's section conjecture for curves of index 1' (arXiv:2305.10088) proves new unconditional cases (twisted forms of index 1 for curves with faithful non-cyclic p-group actions; existence of a finite extension/étale cover satisfying the conjecture for any hyperbolic curve over a finitely generated field) but was submitted 17 May 2023, before the frozen revision date, with no later version — so it is out of the window entirely (not even open_stale-eligible, since it's a partial case, not a resolution). (2) Xu's 'Section conjectures over C and Kodaira fibrations' (arXiv:2407.03248, submitted 3 July 2024, latest v3 20 October 2025) proves topological/Hodge-theoretic analogues of the injectivity part hold, but explicitly shows the topological analogue of the surjectivity part FAILS for families of curves/Jacobians — this is a variant (a different question posed over C with topological/Hodge structure replacing Galois-theoretic structure), not a case of the stated conjecture over finitely-generated fields with the absolute Galois group, so it doesn't count under the scope rule (§3.1). (3) Miller-Wickelgren-Zerbes-style or similar toric section conjecture work (arXiv:2409.07923, 'Section conjecture for the toric fundamental group', v1 12 September 2024, with a v5 September 2026 correcting 'a serious mistake spotted by Y. Hoshi and A. Tamagawa') is again a stated variant (toric fundamental group in place of the full etale fundamental group) rather than the conjecture as given. (4) arXiv:2604.26131 (t-birational/toric refinements) is likewise a variant reduction, not the main conjecture. None of these sources, nor the Betts-Stix Annals paper 'Galois sections and p-adic period mappings' (2025), nor any lab announcement, blog digestion, or Lean/Coq repository I could find, mentions any AI system's involvement in any capacity. The Wikipedia article itself (English, current) remains a stub with no status update beyond attribution to Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings. I am satisfied this is a genuine 'nothing happened' case for the conjecture as stated, with an active but off-scope periphery of variants and pre-window partial cases.
competing_reading: One could argue Bresciani's index-1 result should be recorded even though it predates the window, since some readers might expect any 'case settled' language to appear regardless of date; I excluded it strictly per the window rule in §2.1. One could also argue the toric/birational and complex-analytic variants are close enough in spirit to count as 'cases' rather than 'related problems', since they use the same fundamental-group machinery; but they change the objects (topological/Hodge fundamental group over C, or toric fundamental group) rather than restricting the class of curves/fields in the original statement, so per §3.1 they are variants, not cases.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement, dated after 26 January 2024, proving the section conjecture (injectivity and surjectivity) for a genuinely broader/unconditional class of complete smooth curves over finitely-generated fields with the original Galois-theoretic fundamental-group formulation — as opposed to a change of the ambient category (C-analytic, toric, birational) — would settle a `partial` classification; any AI-authorship claim would require an explicit statement from the paper's authors describing what the system produced.
